chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Riab, from Misma', Abu Sayyar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Sayyar! The state of the one in Ihram is constricted. So whoever kisses his wife without desire while he is in Ihram, upon him is the blood of a sheep. And whoever kisses his wife with desire and discharges semen, upon him is a camel, and he seeks forgiveness of his Lord. And whoever touches his wife with his hand while in Ihram with desire, upon him is the blood of a sheep. And whoever looks at his wife with a lustful look and discharges semen, upon him is a camel. And whoever touches his wife or holds her close without desire, there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.جَزُور: A camel (a heavier type of financial expiation)
key_terms.دَمُ شَاة: Blood of a sheep (a type of financial expiation)
key_terms.لَازَمَهَا: Held her close / remained attached to her

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim in Ihram who kisses or touches his wife?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the financial expiations (dam) for a pilgrim in Ihram engaging in intimacy, distinguishing between acts performed with lust (shahwah) versus those without. The ruling prescribes a sheep for minor lustful contact or non-ejaculatory kissing, a camel for acts leading to ejaculation, and no penalty for non-lustful touch, reflecting the juristic principle that desire intensifies the breach of Ihram sanctity. This hadith is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the gradation of penalties based on the degree of sensory engagement and sexual arousal during the sacred state.

en.hubeali: Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Misma’a Abu Sayyar who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘O Abu Sayyar! The state of the one in Ihraam is constricted. So the one who kisses his wife upon other than desire and he was in Ihraam, so upon him is blood of a sheep; and the one who kisses his wife upon desire, so he discharges semen, so upon him would be a camel, and he should seek Forgiveness of his Lordazwj. And the one who touches his wife with his hand upon desire and he is in Ihraam, so upon him is blood of a sheep. And the one who looks at his wife with a lustful look, so he discharges semen, so upon him would be a camel. And the one who touches his wife, or holds her from without desire, so there is nothing upon him’.
en.sarwar: 4. Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Misma’ abu Sayyar who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once said to me, ‘O abu Sayyar the condition of one in the state of Ihram is restricted. If one kisses his wife without lust while in the state of Ihram, he owes one sheep; if one does so with lust and discharges semen, he owes a Jazur (slaughtering a camel) and must ask his Lord for forgiveness. If one touches his wife with his hand while he is in the state of Ihram with lust, he owes one sheep. If one looks at his wife with lust and ejaculates semen, he owes one Jazur. However, if one touches his wife or holds without lust there is not anything on him.’”
